name: Modular Meta-RL Agent
analogy: Think of it as a trading desk with several specialists, one for trends, one for fading moves, one for thin markets and one for breakouts. A dispatcher watches the tape and decides how much weight to give each specialist at every bar, and a new specialist can join without retraining the rest.

steps.title: Read the bar through a shared encoder
steps.description: A shared front end turns the bar's features into a compact description of the market state. Every specialist works from the same description, which saves effort.
steps.inExample: The 35 base features of the 13:40 bar become a 16-number description.

steps.title: Let each module give its own opinion
steps.description: Every module in the library is a small policy with its own specialty. Each gives its own preference over the possible positions.
steps.inExample: The trend module leans long at 60 percent, the fading module leans long at 30 percent, the thin-market module at 33 percent and the breakout module at 55 percent.

steps.title: Let the router weigh the modules
steps.description: A small router network reads the same description and assigns a weight to each module. The weights add up to 100 percent, so they say how much each specialist is trusted right now.
steps.inExample: The router weights are trend 55 percent, fading 25 percent, thin market 5 percent and breakout 15 percent.

steps.title: Blend the opinions into one decision
steps.description: The module preferences are combined using the router weights, giving one blended preference over positions. A sparse variant uses only the top few modules to save time.
steps.inExample: The blend gives long 50 percent, flat 28 percent and short 22 percent.

steps.title: Train everything together with a balance penalty
steps.description: Modules and router are trained from the reward on the blended decisions. A penalty prevents the router from sending every bar to the same module early on, which would leave the others unused.
steps.inExample: Over a training fold each module receives a non-trivial share of bars rather than one module taking nearly all of them.

steps.title: Add or replace a module later
steps.description: A new module for a newly identified condition can join the library, and only the router has to adapt. The existing, validated modules are left as they are.
steps.inExample: A fifth module for the first five minutes after a news release is added and the router learns when to call on it.

useFor.example: Keeping separate trend, mean-reversion and low-liquidity modules on 5-minute MNQ bars, with the router picking the right mix.
Adding a module for the opening five minutes without disturbing modules already validated on walk-forward folds.

useFor.task: Sharing one feature extractor across instruments
useFor.example: Using a common encoder for MNQ and ES while keeping instrument-specific modules.

useFor.task: Auditing which logic drove each bar
useFor.example: Reading the router weights bar by bar to see whether trades came from the trend module or the breakout module.

useFor.task: Bounded cost as the library grows
useFor.example: Using sparse routing so that only the top two modules run on each live bar.

avoidWhen: You have one steady market and little data; a single policy or a boosted tree has fewer parts to tune and no router to collapse.
You cannot monitor module usage across folds; without that check the router can quietly collapse onto one module and the library is just one policy in disguise.

example.scenario: At 13:40 on MNQ the agent has four modules: trend, fading, thin market and breakout. The shared encoder describes the bar, the router weighs the modules, and the blended policy states its preference.

input.summary: The bar's features and the four modules' individual opinions.

fields.name: close
fields.meaning: The price at which the newest five-minute bar closed, rounded to the nearest point.

fields.name: average true range, 14 bars
fields.meaning: The typical high-to-low travel of a recent bar.

fields.name: relative strength index, 14 bars
fields.meaning: A momentum reading from 0 to 100; moderately strong.

fields.name: trend module, preference for long
fields.meaning: How strongly the trend specialist favours a long position.

fields.name: fading module, preference for long
fields.meaning: How strongly the mean-reversion specialist favours a long position.

fields.name: thin-market module, preference for long
fields.meaning: How strongly the low-liquidity specialist favours a long position.

fields.name: breakout module, preference for long
fields.meaning: How strongly the breakout specialist favours a long position.

output.summary: The router's weights and the blended preference over positions.

fields.name: router weights
fields.value: trend 55 percent, fading 25 percent, thin market 5 percent, breakout 15 percent
fields.meaning: How much the dispatcher trusts each specialist on this bar.

fields.name: blended share long
fields.meaning: The weighted combination of the modules' long preferences: 55 percent of 60, plus 25 percent of 30, plus 5 percent of 33, plus 15 percent of 55.

fields.name: blended share flat
fields.meaning: The weighted combination of the modules' preference for staying out.

fields.name: blended share short
fields.meaning: The weighted combination of the modules' short preferences.

example.reading: Look at the router weights before the blend: a router that gives nearly all of its weight to one module on every bar has collapsed. Compare the whole agent with a single policy of the same size, and judge the blended position after trading costs.
